concepts.name: Similarity of Figures
concepts.description: Two figures are said to be similar if they have the same shape but may differ in size. Corresponding angles are equal, and corresponding sides are proportional.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to distinguish between similar and congruent figures by comparing their corresponding dimensions and angles.

concepts.name: Similarity in Geometry
concepts.description: The concept of similarity helps compare geometric figures and solve problems involving scale, proportion, and measurement.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the importance of similarity in geometric reasoning and practical applications.

concepts.name: Properties of Similar Figures
concepts.description: Similar figures have equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides. Their perimeters are proportional, while their areas are related by the square of the similarity ratio.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify similar figures and determine the ratio of corresponding sides.

concepts.name: Scale Factor
concepts.description: The scale factor represents the ratio between corresponding sides of similar figures. It is used to enlarge or reduce geometric shapes while preserving their proportions.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate and apply the scale factor between similar figures.

concepts.name: AA Similarity Criterion
concepts.description: If two angles of one triangle are equal to two corresponding angles of another triangle, then the triangles are similar.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to prove the similarity of triangles using the AA criterion.

concepts.name: SAS Similarity Criterion
concepts.description: If two sides of one triangle are proportional to two corresponding sides of another triangle and the included angles are equal, then the triangles are similar.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to determine triangle similarity using the SAS criterion.

concepts.name: SSS Similarity Criterion
concepts.description: If the three sides of one triangle are proportional to the three corresponding sides of another triangle, the triangles are similar.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to establish similarity of triangles using the SSS criterion.

concepts.name: Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales' Theorem)
concepts.description: A line drawn parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio. This theorem is fundamental in proving triangle similarity.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to apply the Basic Proportionality Theorem to solve geometric problems.

concepts.name: Converse of Basic Proportionality Theorem
concepts.description: If a line divides two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, then the line is parallel to the third side. This converse is useful for geometric proofs.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to prove whether a line is parallel to a side of a triangle using proportional relationships.

concepts.name: Applications of Similarity
concepts.description: Triangle similarity is widely used to determine unknown lengths, heights, distances, and proportional relationships in geometric constructions and real-life situations.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to solve geometric and real-life problems using properties of similar triangles.

concepts.name: Key Concepts of Triangles
concepts.description: This chapter consolidates the concepts of similar figures, similarity criteria, proportionality theorems, and their applications in solving geometric problems.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to select appropriate similarity criteria and proportionality principles to solve problems involving triangles.
